document_check.note: Opwonya J, Wang C, Jang K-M, Lee K, Kim JI, Kim JU. Inhibitory Control of Saccadic Eye Movements and Cognitive Impairment in Mild Cognitive Impairment. Front Aging Neurosci 2022;14:871432. It is a primary oculomotor experiment comparing 79 MCI patients with 170 healthy controls, all native Korean (p10). This matches the cited context.

cited_result: The review cites the study only as a primary MCI-versus-control oculomotor experiment. The principal result appraised is the group difference in saccade parameters: longer prosaccade latency, a lower proportion of correct responses, and more inhibition and uncorrected errors in antisaccade and No-go trials in MCI than in healthy controls (pp5-6).
tool_reason: The result compares a measured characteristic (saccade performance) between diagnostic groups at a single time point, which is the JBI analytical cross-sectional case. There is no follow-up, no reference-standard accuracy analysis and no model.

domains.rationale: Criteria for both groups are stated: controls had CDR 0, normal cognition and a normal MRI; MCI cases met Petersen criteria with CDR 0.5 and a z-score below -1.5. Reasons for exclusion are given (AD, colour blindness, poor vision, failed calibration).

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: MCI participants met the Petersen criteria (Petersen, 2004) and had a CDR score of 0.5.

domains.rationale: Demographics are reported (Table 1, p4), but the recruitment source, setting (clinic or community), recruitment period and how controls were identified are not. I searched the Methods and Discussion for recruitment site, dates and sampling procedure and found none.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: In this study, 274 subjects participated, and we excluded nine subjects because they were diagnosed with AD.

domains.domain: 3. Exposure (group membership) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: Group membership was assigned by clinical interview with CDR and norm-referenced SNSB II scores.

signalling.question: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: All the participants were examined by a clinical interview, which included the assessment of the clinical dementia rating (CDR).

domains.domain: 4. Objective, standard criteria for the condition
domains.rationale: Petersen criteria, CDR 0.5 and z-scores below -1.5 against age-, education- and sex-specific norms were used. Only controls are described as having a normal MRI, which may make the controls unusually healthy and widen group differences.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: Their neuropsychological test z scores were below -1.5 on at least one of ﬁve domain tests according to age-, education-, and sex-speciﬁc norms.

domains.rationale: Age, sex and years of education are named as covariates, and Table 1 compares them between groups.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: We examined the relationships of neuropsychological domains and saccade responses using partial correlation adjusted for age, sex, and years of education.

domains.rationale: Adjustment was applied only to the correlation analyses. The group comparisons (the principal result) used unadjusted t-tests, although MCI cases were older (73.3 vs 71.5 years, p = 0.069; Table 1, p4). Controls are called 'age-matched' (p1), but no matching procedure is described.

signalling.question: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?
signalling.quote: We carried out t tests, and Pearson’s r correlations analyses.

domains.rationale: Saccades were recorded with a 300 Hz Tobii Pro Spectrum and a chin rest, and responses were classified by an automated area-of-interest algorithm with pre-set thresholds based on published definitions (pp3-4). Participants needed at least 50% valid trials per condition, so sample sizes varied by outcome (p5).

signalling.question: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: Saccadic eye movements were recorded using a Tobii Pro spectrum system (Tobii Technology AB, Stockholm, Sweden)

domains.rationale: About 20 saccade parameters were compared with t-tests without correction for multiple comparisons. Some reported statistics do not match their p-values: t(226) = 3.33 is reported as p = 0.01 (p6), and t(233) = 0.453 as p = 0.964 (p6).

signalling.question: Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
signalling.quote: In the AS paradigm, patients with MCI had a smaller proportion of correct responses (t (226) = 3.33, p = 0.01) than HC.

overall: High risk of bias (JBI analytical cross-sectional checklist; item 6 is 'No' under the review's rule)
overall_rationale: The cited MCI-versus-control differences come from unadjusted t-tests, although age, sex and education were identified as relevant and the MCI group was older. The recruitment setting is not described. Controls had to have a normal MRI, which may make them unusually healthy, and many comparisons were made without multiplicity control, with some statistics inconsistent. The measurement of the condition and of eye movements is sound.

applicability.rationale: The review states the sample is Korean, and the authors note that eye movements may vary by culture and ethnicity (p10).
